questions.scenario: You are playing a business simulation or strategy game. What is your playstyle?

options.text: The Auditor: I balance my resources perfectly and track every single coin spent.
The Hustler: I buy items when they are cheap and sell them fast for a quick profit.
The Tycoon: I save up to buy out other players' companies and build an empire.
The Survivor: I build a massive emergency fund and prepare for any random game disaster.
The Innovator: I write a script or build an automated bot to manage my economy and farm resources for me.
None of these.

questions.scenario: If you were to watch a movie about money, which plot sounds the most exciting?

options.text: A brilliant detective-style accountant uncovers a massive corporate fraud hidden in the numbers.
A fast-paced thriller about a young genius making millions in minutes on the chaotic stock market.
A high-stakes drama about negotiating a multi-billion dollar company buyout in a luxury skyscraper.
A tense movie where an expert calculates the odds of a natural disaster and races to protect the city's assets.
A tech-thriller about a coder who builds a revolutionary AI that disrupts the global banking and payment system.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Your friends are planning a big group trip. What is your role?

options.text: Creating the ultimate spreadsheet to track everyone's share so nobody pays a rupee extra.
Hunting for flash sales and jumping on flight tickets the second prices drop.
Convincing everyone to pitch in a bit more so we can rent a massive luxury villa instead of normal rooms.
Making sure everyone has travel insurance and keeping a backup fund in case someone loses their wallet.
Setting up a digital shared wallet or finding a smart app to automate splitting and paying all the bills.
None of these.

questions.scenario: If you could have a 'Financial Superpower', what would it be?

options.text: Instantly spotting math errors and legal loopholes in any document just by looking at it.
Predicting the exact price of gold, stocks, or Bitcoin for the next 24 hours.
The power of ultimate persuasion—getting billionaires to invest in your massive ideas.
Seeing the future to prevent accidents, disasters, and financial losses before they happen.
The ability to code perfect algorithms and create the ultimate unhackable digital currency.
None of these.

questions.scenario: You just won a decent amount of cash in a school competition. What do you do?

options.text: Put it in a secure bank account and strictly budget how to spend it over the next few months.
Buy limited-edition sneakers or gadgets to re-sell them later for double the price.
Partner with a friend and use the money to start a profitable mini-business at school.
Keep a big chunk of it hidden away safely just in case my phone or laptop breaks and needs fixing.
Invest it in buying servers, domain names, or software to build a new app or digital product.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Which of these desk setups or toolkits sounds the coolest to you?

options.text: Neatly stacked ledger files, a high-end calculator, and color-coded highlighters.
Six curved monitors showing live, fast-moving green and red charts and graphs.
A sleek laptop, a tailored suit, and a VIP contact list on a premium smartphone.
Complex statistical models and probability simulation software running on a tablet.
A dual-monitor coding setup running Python scripts, API integrations, and blockchain nodes.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Your school is hosting a massive carnival. Where are you during the event?

options.text: Sitting in the back office, making sure the cash collected perfectly matches the tickets sold.
Changing the price of cold drinks on the spot depending on how sunny it gets to maximize profit.
I was the one who negotiated with local businesses to sponsor the biggest Ferris wheel we've ever had.
Checking the safety harnesses on the rides and making sure the first-aid team is ready.
Setting up QR code payment systems and a custom digital token app so students don't have to carry cash.
None of these.

questions.scenario: When playing a board game like Monopoly with friends, what is your winning strategy?

options.text: Never making a mistake as the Banker and tracking everyone's cash perfectly.
Trading properties aggressively, offering quick deals to confuse my opponents and win big.
Saving up to buy the most expensive properties and bankrupting everyone in one massive hit.
Always keeping enough cash on hand just in case I land on a high-rent space or go to jail.
Convincing the group to play a digital version instead where banking and transactions are fully automated.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Finance jobs are tough. Which of these 'boring/hard' tasks can you tolerate the most?

options.text: Going through hundreds of receipts to find why the budget is missing 10 rupees.
Staring at screens at 2 AM trying to time the perfect split-second moment to buy an asset.
Working 80-hour weeks putting together a massive 100-page pitch presentation for a CEO.
Reading 50 pages of boring legal terms and conditions to find one tiny loophole.
Staring at code for hours trying to debug a financial transaction system that keeps failing by one decimal point.
None of these.

questions.scenario: In your friend group, what is your ultimate financial title?

options.text: The Auditor (The organized, detail-oriented money manager).
The Trader (The risk-taker who spots quick opportunities).
The Dealmaker (The persuasive, big-picture negotiator).
The Protector (The safe, prepared, and secure planner).
The Innovator (The tech-savvy builder of digital money solutions).
None of these.
